13324dee-91c7-423d-a521-b4c101382449.recap: Bloomberg's Credit Edge hosts Alberto Gallo, CIO of Andromeda Capital, who frames rising long-end yields (US, UK, Japan) as an 'impossible trinity' problem: governments can't simultaneously run wartime-level deficits, keep currencies stable, and hold yields down. His base case is that currency debasement comes first (dovish central banks hiking less than needed, sticky above-target inflation for six years), but a credit crunch could follow if Japan's BOJ is forced to hike faster, pulling Japanese savers out of Treasuries/Bunds and into JGBs. On credit, Gallo describes a 'Jenga tower' of debt, with government bonds at the base and a new $3 trillion private credit layer at the top, heavily concentrated (over 40%, per IMF data) in tech/software financing the AI capex buildout, much of it negative-free-cash-flow and intangible-heavy. He argues investors aren't paid for the risk (200-300bp spreads funding IG-adjacent economics) and that private credit's non-mark-to-market structure hides losses (Schrödinger's default via PIK toggles) that could transmit contagion through life insurers (Athene, Global Atlantic) to state guarantee funds and taxpayers rather than banks. Andromeda is broadly short data centers, private credit managers, and insurers via bonds/CDS/equity, while staying long convertibles and real-asset sectors (defense, mining, energy, infrastructure) and gold. He also flags record CDX IG/HY long positioning (99.9th percentile) as a latent risk if spreads (currently near 30-year tights) reprice, and sees Ukraine sovereign/corporate debt as a contrarian EM opportunity given hard-commodity exposure and EU accession prospects.
terms: CDS -- credit default swap, a derivative providing protection against a bond or loan default
CDX -- the North American corporate credit default swap index (investment grade and high yield versions)
PIK -- payment-in-kind, where interest is paid by issuing more debt/accrual rather than cash
SPV -- special purpose vehicle, a legally separate entity used to isolate financial risk or hold assets/debt off a parent's balance sheet
LBO -- leveraged buyout, acquisition of a company financed largely with borrowed money
BDC -- business development company, a closed-end investment vehicle that lends to or invests in private middle-market companies

a12a9081-0f03-4073-b09e-6ddee4a031e6.one_liner: A 100-to-zero private credit markdown at Blue Owl (Loporex), plus fresh fraud allegations at Radiant World and a wave of US issuers fleeing to European and even New Zealand bond markets to dodge hyperscaler-crowded dollar issuance, together read as a credit cycle turning against private credit valuations and dollar funding availability.
a12a9081-0f03-4073-b09e-6ddee4a031e6.recap: The piece centers on Blue Owl's BDC (OBDC) writing a senior secured loan to Loporex, an adhesive-liner maker owned by Pamplona Capital, from par (and junior debt near 90) down to near zero within months, after Moody's declared default and flagged possible Chapter 11. The author argues this exemplifies a structural private-credit problem: illiquid loans are marked by internal models rather than market trades, so deterioration doesn't show up as gradual price declines like public debt but arrives suddenly as a cliff from 100 to 0, echoing Renovo Home Partners' identical pattern last November (BlackRock/MidCap Financial marks at par weeks before bankruptcy despite a PIK restructuring already in place). A second thread covers Radiant World, an iron-ore trader hit with a worldwide freezing order after a Jefferies-affiliated Point Bonita fund alleged a fraudulent scheme involving falsified invoices and contracts, raising due-diligence questions reminiscent of Tricolor and First Brands. A third thread describes borrowers migrating away from a dollar bond market congested by massive hyperscaler debt issuance for AI infrastructure: a record single-day wave of US corporate issuance in Europe (Amazon in sterling, Uber in euros), and Korea's Eximbank (Kexim) returning to New Zealand's Kauri market after nine years to escape crowding-out effects. The author ties these together as one cycle: lenders' marks are proving unreliable while borrowers' assumed ability to refinance is eroding, and BDC share prices trading at discounts to NAV reflect market skepticism toward reported valuations.
terms: BDC -- Business Development Company, a publicly traded or non-traded vehicle that lends to and invests in mostly private middle-market companies
PIK -- Payment-in-Kind, where interest is paid by issuing more debt/principal rather than cash
NAV -- Net Asset Value, the reported per-share value of a fund's underlying holdings
non-accrual -- a loan status where a lender stops recognizing interest income because repayment is doubtful
